name: Account-abuse / bot-defence
topic: Beava's current market position - competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against, evaluated against the use-case map in ../beava-use-cases/

competitive_landscape.incumbents: Generic real-time stack: Redis (counters + Lua, plus Redis Stack with Bloom / CMS / Top-K modules) is the overwhelming default for hand-rolled per-IP / per-fingerprint velocity at every scale below hyperscaler; the Apr 2024 RSALv2/SSPLv1 relicense and the Linux Foundation's BSD-3-Clause Valkey fork (Apr 2024, AWS/Google/Oracle-backed, default in Ubuntu 26.04) split this default into a license-clean Valkey path and a relicensed-Redis path. Aerospike at very high cardinality (Cloudflare-style edge data plane). DragonflyDB / Memcached for simpler counters. Cloudflare Durable Objects for serverless-edge rate counters (soft-limit ~1k req/s per DO, sharding required above). Flink / Materialize / RisingWave for buyers who already have Kafka and want SQL-on-streams (RisingWave publishes an explicit 'Real-Time Features for Account Takeover Detection' blog). Online feature stores (Tecton-now-Databricks, Hopsworks, Chalk, Fennel-now-Databricks, Feast) are an awkward fit at the edge - they target ML serving from a central warehouse, not in-line auth / WAF decisions. Custom in-Rust services on top of RocksDB or Sled are common at the very top end (Cloudflare, Fastly, Akamai internal stacks). Counter-style hand-rolled Redis+Lua remains the most common 'rolled-own' shape beava could replace.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Bot-management / fraud-prevention vendors are the named, productised incumbents here, NOT the data backend - beava more naturally sits underneath one of these vendors or an in-house equivalent than replaces them. Active 2025-2026 players: Cloudflare Bot Management (Enterprise-only add-on, ~$5k/mo entry, on top of multi-billion-req/day ML training data; Cloudflare reported weekly AI-agent requests more than doubled in Jan 2026; 'Per-customer defenses' shipped Nov 2025; Web Bot Auth + HTTP Message Signatures launched at Agents Week 2026). DataDome ($81.1M total funding, $42M Series C 2023 led by InfraVia; <2ms inline; ~$1,990-$4,000/mo for 10-30M req/mo published; Forrester Wave Leader; 350B+ attacks/year). HUMAN Security (post-PerimeterX merger Jul 2022 at ~$1.5B combined valuation, 450+ employees, 500+ customers, $100M+ ARR, $100M Blackstone debt + $100M growth round WestCap/NightDragon). Kasada ($2,500-$4,000/mo for 10-20M req). Arkose Labs (launched unified Arkose Titan platform Jan 2026 - first vendor explicitly framing 'AI agent vs human vs bot' as the new axis, with device intelligence Mar 2026; Arkose research: 97% of enterprise leaders expect a material AI-agent-driven security/fraud incident within 12 months). Castle.io (behavioral integrity, shipped no-code Cloudflare Worker integration May 2025 - 'edge to in-app' positioning; runs 'Roll your own bot detection' Oct 2025 content series explicitly to surface in-house-build buyers). Fingerprint.com (device intelligence, $77M total raised through Series C, 175% revenue growth reported Apr 2025 over two years, then 65% ARR growth Feb 2026 with 1B+ device IDs/month; ships 'Velocity Signals' product - per-VisitorID / per-LinkedID / per-IP counters at 5m / 1h / 24h - the closest commercial analog to beava's primitive shape). Akamai Bot Manager + Noname Security (acquired $450M Jun 2024 - the biggest single M&A signal of enterprise demand in this category). hCaptcha (Enterprise risk-scoring platform; Google reCAPTCHA pivoted to GCP-only pricing 2025 with free tier dropped from 1M to 10k/mo, driving migration). Cloudflare Turnstile (free <=1M req/mo - the no-budget hyperscaler bundle). F5 Distributed Cloud Bot Defense (formerly Shape). Imperva (Thales). Netacea. Cequence ($100M raised). Wallarm ($55M Series C Jul 2025, Toba Capital lead, 'API security for the AI era'). Salt Security. 42Crunch. Stytch Intelligent Rate Limiting (2025). On the data-backend side specifically (where beava actually competes): Redis (counters + Lua + Bloom/CMS/Top-K) remains the rolled-own default, with Valkey now the procurement-clean OSS fork.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Mixed and rapidly shifting. The PRODUCT-level incumbents (Cloudflare BM, DataDome, HUMAN, Kasada, Arkose Titan, Castle, Fingerprint, Akamai BM, hCaptcha Enterprise, F5, Imperva, Netacea, Cequence, Wallarm, Salt, 42Crunch, Stytch) are uniformly proprietary commercial SaaS. The BACKEND-level incumbent (Redis) is the locked buyer filter: Redis 7.4+ is RSALv2/SSPLv1 dual-licensed (non-OSI, considered non-OSS by Fedora/Debian/AWS/Google/Ubuntu); Valkey BSD-3-Clause (Linux Foundation, AWS/Google/Oracle-backed, default 'redis-server' package in Ubuntu 26.04) is now the procurement-clean drop-in. Redis 8 (May 2025) re-introduced an AGPLv3 option as part of a tri-license but Valkey continues to win the cloud-default migration. Beava's Apache-2.0 + no open-core posture is a real wedge against any 'rolled-own on Redis' buyer who got caught flat-footed by the relicense, AND against the proprietary-only vendor incumbents who want to embed a feature backend without depending on a competitor's managed cloud (Castle / Fingerprint / Datadome would all prefer Apache-2.0 over a Redis Source-Available dependency). License posture is now a HARD filter, not a preference, in this segment.
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: High. This is one of beava's most threatened segments. Cloudflare bundles Bot Management ($5k/mo Enterprise add-on), WAF rate limiting (free in zone plans), Turnstile (free <=1M/mo CAPTCHA), Workers Rate Limiting API, and Durable Objects (purpose-built for cross-PoP synchronised counters) into a single subscription that any Cloudflare-fronted enterprise already pays for. Cloudflare's Jan 2026 Agents Week shipped Web Bot Auth + HTTP Message Signatures + per-customer behavioural baselines, locking incumbents further in. AWS WAF rate-based rules, AWS Bot Control, GCP reCAPTCHA Enterprise (now GCP-only since 2025 transition), and Azure Front Door / Application Gateway rate-limiting are all 'good-enough' bundled alternatives for enterprises that have already chosen a hyperscaler. The Castle-on-Cloudflare May 2025 integration ('connect an API token, Castle deploys a Worker') and DataDome's CDN-agnostic <2ms edge integrations actually deepen the bundling threat by piggybacking on Cloudflare reach. The buyers beava can still win are explicitly (a) non-Cloudflare-fronted infrastructure (origin-only / multi-cloud / on-prem), (b) bot-management VENDORS who want to embed a feature backend without becoming Cloudflare-dependent (Castle, Fingerprint, DataDome, Kasada), and (c) the 'rolled-own on Redis' in-house teams that the Castle 'Roll your own bot detection' Oct 2025 blog series is explicitly targeting. The bundling pressure is structurally higher than in real-time feature stores (H1) because the WAF / edge layer is already a CDN concern.
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: Producers in this segment are edge proxies and auth services, NOT Kafka/Spark pipelines - this is a strong fit for beava's push-on-event model. Expected upstreams: Cloudflare Workers (Rate Limiting API + Durable Objects), Fastly Compute, Envoy (access-log filter, ext_proc, Lua filter, Wasm filter), Nginx (njs, Lua), Caddy, HAProxy, Kong (Lua/Go plugins), Tyk (Go/JS middleware), Apigee (JS/Java callouts), AWS API Gateway (Lambda authoriser, WAF rate-based rules), Coraza WAF (proxy-wasm), OPA/Envoy plugin. Auth services / IDPs (Auth0, Okta, WorkOS, Stytch, Descope, Curity) emitting login_attempt / signup / password_reset / otp_request. Mobile/web SDKs pushing device-fp + behavioural events directly. Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 fits Workers / serverless producers; framed-TCP :8081 fits the high-throughput Envoy / Nginx / Kong / auth-service path. The Kafka-first feature-store assumption (Feast/Tecton/Hopsworks) is REVERSED here - bot defence buyers explicitly do not want a broker hop on the inline-decision path, which is exactly what beava sells. The friction is on the CLIENT side: gateway buyers (Cloudflare, Kong, Tyk, Envoy) live in Rust / Go / C++ / Lua / Wasm, not Python; beava ships a Python SDK + a language-agnostic wire (TCP+msgpack, HTTP+JSON), but does not yet ship Rust / Go / Lua / Wasm client SDKs which is the gap for this market.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. The dominant pattern is a deterministic rules layer (per-IP failure_ratio > X, per-(api_key x route) rate > Y, per-fingerprint signups > Z per hour) combined with an ML risk scorer (XGBoost / LightGBM / deep model) consuming the same beava features. Concretely: Cloudflare Bot Management is an ML scorer with a rules layer on top; Coraza / OWASP CRS is pure rules; Castle / Fingerprint / DataDome / HUMAN / Kasada / Arkose Titan are scorer-plus-rules products. Beava as a pure feature backend stays decoupled from the scorer - natural seam, identical role across all named incumbents.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: Seven concrete reasons a buyer in this segment would pick beava over Redis-on-Lua or one of the proprietary product incumbents today: (1) Single binary, no Kafka / Flink / Redis cluster - fits the per-PoP / per-cluster sidecar topology this market has standardised on (Cloudflare Workers, Fastly Compute, Envoy sidecar, Castle's Cloudflare Worker pattern). (2) ~60 first-class aggregation primitives (counters, n_unique HLL, velocity, rate, distribution, distance, entropy, last-N) cover the per-(IP, key, route, status_class, fingerprint) features this domain literally lives on, WITHOUT writing Lua / Wasm / Flink SQL. Fingerprint.com's 'Velocity Signals' product (per-VisitorID/LinkedID/IP at 5m/1h/24h) is essentially the productised form of one slice of what beava ships as a generic primitive set - strong external validation of the shape. (3) Sub-millisecond TCP+msgpack get / batch_get sits inside the <5ms inline-decision budget the WAAP market is measured on (DataDome publishes <2ms; Cloudflare DO ~1k req/s per shard). (4) Apache-2.0 with NO open-core - attractive both to gateway vendors (Kong / Tyk / Apigee / Zuplo) and to bot-management vendors (Castle / Fingerprint / DataDome / Kasada) that want to embed a feature backend WITHOUT depending on a competitor's managed cloud OR a Redis Source-Available dependency. This is a real wedge specifically post-Apr-2024 Redis relicense. (5) Push-on-event model maps directly to how proxies already emit access logs (Envoy access-log filter, Nginx access_log, Coraza audit log) - no broker hop, no broker capex. (6) Composite-key story ((ip x route), (key x status_class), (asn x route), (fp x route), (account_id x ip)) is first-class via @bv.table, not bolted on as a Redis key-naming convention. (7) The 'distances' primitive cleanly expresses impossible-travel on (account_id, last_known_geo), which is otherwise hand-rolled with Redis + Haversine.
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: Concrete gaps blocking adoption in this segment today (derived from use cases 2 and 15b): (1) No TLS / no auth on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 in v0 - disqualifying for any production deployment by a regulated buyer (IDP, PSP, EU PSD3/DORA-regulated firm) or any vendor that needs mTLS between the proxy and the feature backend. This is the single biggest blocker; effectively limits beava today to in-VPC / behind-mTLS-proxy deployments. (2) No triggers / 'callback when counter crosses threshold' - bot defence is INHERENTLY event-driven ('fire CAPTCHA when this IP's 1m failure ratio > 0.4'; 'tighten this api_key's budget when 1m failure_ratio > 0.4'), and polling 20-100 features per inline request just to threshold them wastes round-trips. This is among the most-cited gaps for the domain in both use-case write-ups. (3) No in-process sharding - a single tenant beyond ~684k EPS (M4 published) or ~50 GB hot state must be hand-sharded externally; an edge buyer doing global bot management is far beyond one box. (4) No cross-node / cross-PoP feature merge or replication - global rate limiting (Zuplo's pitch, Cloudflare DO's raison d'etre) is not possible without external coordination. (5) Refuse-on-network-FS + in-memory only means each PoP must plan local-disk WAL and bounded cold-start replay; an IP-cardinality blowup during a DDoS-class event could OOM the node. (6) No first-class HLL / Bloom / CMS / Top-K in the documented primitive set (may exist in the 60-primitive count but is not prominently documented for this domain) - the (ip x route) cross-product is naively unbounded and these approximate sketches are the fix. (7) Per-key TTL / sliding-window eviction is not first-class - explosive IP cardinality under DDoS-class events can OOM the box. (8) No multi-tenancy primitives - per-tenant namespaces, quotas, isolation, per-tenant rate-limit accounting required for any WAAP / bot-management vendor serving many customers. (9) No Rust / Go / C++ / Lua / Wasm client SDKs - the buyer ecosystem here lives in proxies, not Python services; the wire is language-agnostic but the SDK matrix is the gap. (10) No secondary indexes / no 'list top-k IPs by failure_ratio in last 5 min' query - limits the SOC / analyst surface. (11) No salted-IP-hash-at-rest / short-default-TTL / documented PII model - GDPR / CCPA buyer requirement.
beava_position_lens.time_to_credible_offering: 3-6mo. The disqualifier list is dominated by infrastructure additions, not data-model rewrites: TLS + token/mTLS auth (item 1) is ~1mo; triggers / threshold-crossing webhooks (item 2) is ~1-2mo and unlocks the most-cited domain gap; HLL/CMS/Top-K documentation + first-class promotion (item 6) is ~2-4 weeks if already present; per-key TTL + multi-tenant namespaces (items 7,8) is ~1-2mo; Rust + Go client SDKs (item 9) is ~1-2mo for two of them. In-process sharding and cross-PoP merge (items 3,4) are 6-12mo+ each but are not required for the bot-management-vendor-embeds-beava motion that is beava's realistic first wedge here - a single-binary regional deployment fits within one box for any non-hyperscaler buyer.

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: Beava-side: NO public users on this use case yet; NO dedicated bot-defence / credential-stuffing / signup-flood / API-abuse demo identified in the repository (closest analog is the generic fraud demo at python/beava/demos/fraud); NO beava-specific Discord / GitHub Discussion threads located on this topic. [uncertain] Beava knows WHO the buyer is (platform / infra / SecOps / edge-eng at IDPs, bot-management vendors, edge/WAAP vendors, API-gateway vendors, large in-house platforms - this is correctly identified in README positioning) and the operator catalogue (counters + n_unique + velocity + distribution + distance + entropy) is a near-exact fit for the published primitive shapes of Fingerprint Velocity Signals and Castle behavioural-velocity-checks. External validation that the SHAPE is right (not that beava itself has traction): Fingerprint's 175% revenue growth over two years (reported Apr 2025) followed by 65% ARR growth Feb 2026 with 1B+ device IDs/month explicitly selling the per-IP/visitor velocity primitive set; Castle's no-code Cloudflare Worker integration May 2025 selling exactly the 'edge + in-app behavioural velocity' shape; Arkose Titan launch Jan 2026 with 97% of enterprise leaders expecting a material AI-agent-driven security/fraud incident within 12 months; Wallarm $55M Series C Jul 2025 on 'API security for the AI era'; DataDome 350B+ attacks/year at <2ms inline; Akamai 193B credential-stuffing requests in 2024 (up 66% YoY); Sumsub Identity Fraud Report 2025-2026 finding 76% of fraud takes place AFTER KYC (i.e. post-onboarding, in the continuous-monitoring layer beava feeds); Auth0 reporting up to 69% of daily logins suspected stuffing on attack days. The market validation is overwhelming; the beava-specific traction is zero.
evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Compete (with caveats). Lead-eligible on technical fit (the operator catalogue is a near-exact shape match for what Fingerprint and Castle productise), market urgency (2026 agentic-AI bot wave, post-KYC fraud shift, Cloudflare Agents Week, Akamai-Noname M&A, Wallarm Series C, Arkose Titan launch all in the last 12 months), and Apache-2.0 wedge against both Redis post-relicense AND every proprietary product incumbent. Downgraded to Compete because (a) hyperscaler bundling threat is HIGH (Cloudflare BM + Workers + DOs + Turnstile bundle is the buyer-default), (b) zero beava-side traction / no dedicated demo, and (c) the realistic motion is 'feature backend EMBEDDED under a Castle / Fingerprint / DataDome / in-house equivalent' not 'beava replaces Cloudflare Bot Management'. Pursue actively as a wedge IF beava ships: TLS+auth, threshold-crossing triggers, prominently-documented HLL/CMS, Rust+Go SDKs, and one credible design-partner-shaped demo (impossible-travel + per-IP velocity + per-fingerprint velocity, against a real WAF log replay).
